candidates.title: LoopFit: Retrofitting Pretrained Diffusion Transformers with Recurrent Refinement
candidates.abstract: Scaling inference computation offers a way to improve diffusion transformers (DiTs), but taking more sampling steps leaves the depth of each denoising prediction unchanged. Recurrently reusing Transformer blocks increases computation within each step, allowing further refinement of hidden representations. candidates.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
candidates.abstract: We propose LoopDVR, a framework for converting pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks. Rather than reducing the network width or depth directly, LoopDVR reuses Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and Transformer decoder, reducing the number of parameters while retaining the original computational structure. However, naively sharing parameters can disrupt the distinct transformations learned at different depths.

candidates.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
candidates.abstract: Looped transformers reuse one block of shared weights along the depth of the network. Recent looped diffusion transformers are trained from scratch, which repeats the full pretraining cost although strong pretrained non-looped diffusion transformers exist. We propose Distill to Loop (Dooop), which distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student whose blocks are initialized from the teacher's. candidates.title: How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective
candidates.abstract: Recurrent-depth models are trained with truncated backpropagation, yet it remains unclear why this works. We show that input injection, commonly used in recurrent-depth models, is exactly Halpern iteration, and that a slowly vanishing stepsize provably converges with a backpropagation window polylogarithmic in the depth.
